articles.title: T-Mobile Taps Bryan Cranston in Bid to Wake Consumers Up to ‘T-Mix’ Plan
articles.summary: We are all about to get a very loud wake-up call from T-Mobile. The telecommunications provider, one of the biggest and most colorful advertisers in the U.S., has dispatched actor Bryan Cranston in a new campaign that may surprise those who have grown familiar with its playful spots featuring…
body: “Come on sleepyheads, it’s up and at ‘em!” Cranston crows in the ad. “Because there’s been a change in plan!” Meanwhile, he sets about rousing people from hotel rooms, airplane seats and bedrooms.
In the commercial, “I represent all the people who need to hear this information,” says Cranston in a recent interview. “Because I was one of them until moments ago.”

The 60-second ad debuts during Amazon Prime Video’s “ Thursday Night Football” and will roll out across national broadcast, streaming, cinema, digital, social media platforms, as well as on radio and out-of-home, says Lucy McLellan, executive vice president and chief brand and communications officer at T-Mobile. And while T-Mobile is known for launching big campaigns, the company will also use digital to launch some bespoke creative that targets specific consumer niches.

The new work, created with a new agency of record, Highdive, will attempt “to reach new audiences who have tuned out the category completely,” says McLellan, and make an effort to “appeal to audiences beyond the millennials that T-Mobile has traditionally appeared to.”

articles.title: Levon Hawke to Star With Anthony Hopkins in Indie Drama ‘Twenty-Seven’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Levon Hawke (“Blink Twice,” “The Crowded Room”) will star opposite Academy Award winner Anthony Hopkins (“The Father”) in the drama “Twenty-Seven.” In the film, written and directed by Gregory Caruso, Hawke portrays a 27-year-old aspiring screenwriter attempting to manage his relationships and his…
body: “I wrote this character hoping someone like Anthony Hopkins would play him. I never imagined it would actually be Anthony Hopkins,” said Caruso. “He brings a mastery to the role I still can’t fully describe, and Levon meets him in every scene with real vulnerability and intelligence. At its heart, ‘Twenty-Seven’ is about the uncertainty of growing up, feeling stuck between where you are and where you want to be, and the people who help you find your way.”

“Twenty-Seven,” from Caruso’s Bristol Pictures, is currently in production in Los Angeles. David Worthen Brooks (“Misty Green,” “Appendage”) will produce alongside Dustin Cook (“Flock of Four,” “The Frontier”).

Caruso’s crew includes director of photography Matthew Pothier (“Mutt”), production designer Emma Rose Mead (“To Leslie”), costume designer Jenny Eagan (“Knives Out”), hair and makeup leads Mandy Artusato and Gina Marie DeAngelis (“One Battle After Another”), editor Aleshka Ferrero (“Euphoria”) and casting director Vickie Thomas (“Michael,” “Misty Green”).

articles.title: ‘George Lucas told me off for wearing lipstick’: Celia Imrie on Traitors, Star Wars and treating the lens like a lover
articles.summary: The actor answers your questions about trapeze lessons, Bond villain ambitions and Michael Caine’s top tips. You looked as if you had such a good time on Celebrity Traitors last year – you had them hanging on your every word. What was it like? Who have you kept in touch with?
body: Kate [Garraway] and I had to go on that Uncloaked thing after. She turned to me and she said: “Oh, but Celia, we’re now all one big happy family, aren’t we?” I said: “Well, frankly, I don’t want to see any of them ever again in the whole of my life,” and everybody laughed. But truthfully, we haven’t really run into each other since. Nevertheless, I think I was with a marvellous company, and I liked them all.

Maria Aitken asked me if I’d like to take part. Some of my friends said: “Oh God, you don’t want to look like a student on television.” I said: “What are you talking about? I’d like to be able to say good morning the way Michael Caine does on film.” I was thrilled to be part of it. One of his famous things was: don’t blink in a closeup. He also said to work out any props the night before, and something rather marvellous: that you have to think of the camera as your lover. The camera is ready to love you, so you must reciprocate. I’ve remembered all of that.

articles.title: Raise the Red Lantern review – Gong Li gives a decade-defining performance in an addictively ruthless masterpiece
articles.summary: Gong simmers with rage, loneliness and humiliation as the ‘fourth mistress’ navigating the intimate political savagery of her husband’s compound in Zhang Yimou’s 1991 drama.
body: Gong Li gives one of the great performances of the 1990s as Songlian, a beautiful, intelligent young woman in 1920s China who is forced to abandon her university studies after just six months because her father has died and there is no longer money for the fees. In the unforgettable opening scene, which unfolds with a single unbroken shot of Gong’s pale face, incandescent with shock and pain, Songlian announces to her callous stepmother (who remains off camera) that she is ready to accept marriage – and then her eyes brim with tears. Her suppressed rage, loneliness and humiliation are to simmer below the surface for the rest of the film.

articles.title: Saudi-Backed LIV Golf, After Five Years of Trying to Challenge PGA Tour, Is Shutting Down
articles.summary: LIV Golf, the pro-golfing startup venture whose biggest investor had been the sovereign wealth fund of Saudi Arabia, is shutting down after it couldn’t reach an agreement with a new investor on a bankruptcy reorganization.
body: After the Saudis exited, LIV Golf had proposed a recapitalization transaction with BC Partners Advisors through its voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey. However, according to a statement from the league, “the relevant parties were ultimately unable to reach a consensual resolution of certain outstanding terms of the transaction.”

As such, LIV Golf announced that it intends to liquidate its assets and wind down the business, but added that “the company will remain open to, and continue to consider, any value-maximizing alternatives with third parties that may arise.”

BC Partners Credit had proposed investing $300 million into LIV Golf but deal talks fell apart. In a statement, the financial firm said, “BC Partners Credit supported a transaction that aligned the interests of players and investors, offering a credible path toward building a sustainable future for LIV Golf. While there was great support for the league, we are disappointed that mutually acceptable terms could not be reached among the various stakeholders.”

articles.title: Warner Records Hit With Executive Layoffs
articles.summary: Warner Records was hit with approximately a dozen layoffs across the company this week, including executive marketing VPs Victoria “Torie” Mason and Dalia Ganz and senior VP of publicity Fount Lynch, sources confirm to Variety.
body: The news was first reported by Country Aircheck; reps for the company had no comment.

The moves continue a long and far-reaching series of layoffs since CEO Robert Kyncl officially took the helm in January of 2023. It seems this round was a latter part of the $170 million in staff cuts announced in July of 2025, which the company said was the final stage of the restructuring, although it is also possibly related to the departure of longtime co-chair and COO Tom Corson, who was elevated to COO of the parent company, Warner Music Group, earlier this year.
“Many changes will be implemented in the next three months, with the remainder in fiscal 2026,” Kyncl wrote in a July 2025 memo to the staff, in which he laid out the company’s priorities.

“In an ever-changing industry, we must continue to supercharge our capabilities in long-term artist, songwriter, and catalog development,” he wrote. “That’s why this company was created in the first place, it’s what we’ve always been best at, and it’s how we’ll differentiate ourselves in the future.”

articles.title: ‘Children were wearing fake life jackets’: one Syrian family’s terrifying, 10-year journey
articles.summary: In 2015, two film-makers first met 11-year-old refugee Israa, forced to abandon Aleppo for a new life in Europe, along with her parents and siblings. None of them imagined what would come next.
body: I n 2015, an 11-year-old Syrian girl called Israa matter-of-factly explained how her family would survive if their dinghy sank crossing the sea from Turkey to Greece. Her father would grab her disabled sister; her mother would look after the baby. “And I,” said Israa, a huge smile lighting her face, “I know how to rescue myself.”

Wife-and-husband documentary-makers Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes met Israa while filming a BBC series, Exodus, about refugees trying to reach Europe. Their plan was to follow Israa and her family on their hazardous journey to Germany. But after Israa reached safety, the pair kept filming. Ten years in the making, their documentary, One in a Million, is extraordinary - with echoes of Richard Linklater’s Boyhood and the Up! series. We watch Israa grow up in front of our eyes, from a sunny-natured 11-year-old to a woman, married with a baby of her own.

articles.title: I Play Rocky review – Anthony Ippolito adds knockout sweetness to the story of Stallone’s Hollywood triumph
articles.summary: Portraying the humour, passion and grit that took the actor from bit parts to Oscar glory, this making-of tale is even more mythic than the original movie. For fun, excitement and the transcendental thrill of success, there’s nothing to touch this very enjoyable drama about the making of Sylvester…
body: It is the story of the struggling young Italian-American unknown who’d had some minor acting jobs – including softcore pornography – but wrote a thumpingly good screenplay inspired by the underdog white boxer Chuck Wepner, who briefly knocked Ali down in 1975. With tremendous self-belief, Stallone insisted he play the lead role himself, holding out against vast cash offers to just take the writing credit and let an established star into the ring.

As the man himself, Anthony Ippolito is an eerie likeness of the young Stallone. It’s almost a cine-seance: the same face, the same seductively slurred voice, the same ox-adjacent physique (though not as stacked and defined in 1976 as an unclothed man in a comparable role would need to be now). What is so incredible is that Ippolito is no one-trick pony. In the 2022 Paramount+ miniseries The Offer, about the making of The Godfather, he played the young Al Pacino. That was a stunning likeness, too.

articles.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault
articles.summary: Brand is told to expect a prison sentence "of some length" and faces more rape allegations, it can now be reported.
body: Russell Brand has been convicted of rape and sexual assault, and is now expected to face a substantial prison sentence.
A jury found the entertainer guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, following a four-week trial at Southwark Crown Court in London.
He was found not guilty of two other counts of rape, and one count of attempted indecent assault. The jury deliberated for eight-and-a-half hours.
Brand was taken into custody after the verdicts were delivered, and was refused bail. He is due to be sentenced on Monday.

articles.title: Bonnie Tyler's hometown pays tribute with new mural
articles.summary: Artist Steve Jenkins painted the "important" piece at Skewen Memorial Park, in Neath Port Talbot.
body: A mural of Bonnie Tyler has been unveiled in her hometown as a tribute to the global star "who never forgot her roots".
The Holding Out For a Hero singer, whose real name was Gaynor Hopkins, died in a hospital in Portugal in July, aged 75, after undergoing emergency intestinal surgery earlier this year.
Hundreds lined the streets of Skewen, in Neath Port Talbot, where she was born and raised, to pay their respects on the day of her funeral.
Artist Steve Jenkins, who painted the piece at Skewen Memorial Park, said it was "important" and the "pressure was on" to get the artwork right for the community.

articles.title: ‘The Wizard of Oz’ Was a Big Reference for Doc ‘A Want in Her.’ Now Its Creator Is Moving Into Fiction.
articles.summary: Irish artist-turned-filmmaker Myrid Carten, who won three BIFAs for her feature debut and made the U.K. BAFTA Breakthrough list, talks to THR about her journey so far – and what lies ahead.
body: About 11 months ago, Myrid Carten’s debut feature film, the documentary A Want in Her, an exploration of intergenerational trauma, mental health and addiction, was honored with three British Independent Film Awards ( BIFAs ), namely for best feature documentary, the best debut director – feature documentary, and The Raindance Maverick Award.
On Wednesday, the Irish artist-turned-filmmaker was revealed as a member of the 2026 U.K. BAFTA Breakthrough cohort, supported by Netflix.

On the occasion of her inclusion on the U.K. BAFTA Breakthrough list, Carten talked to THR about her journey behind A Want in Her, just how vulnerable she made herself in the process and what’s next for her.
What led you to take on such a challenging film project, for which you made yourself so vulnerable?
